robotics-cv-basics.q: If a robot needs to identify and locate every car in a parking lot image, which computer vision task is it primarily performing?
options: Image Segmentation
Object Detection
Motion Tracking
Scene Classification
robotics-cv-basics.explanation: Object detection focuses on locating and identifying specific objects within an image.

robotics-cv-basics.q: A robot needs to find the distinct outlines of objects in its environment. Which common computer vision technique would be most appropriate for this purpose?
options: Template Matching
Feature Extraction (SIFT/ORB)
Edge Detection (Canny)
Machine Learning (CNN/YOLO)
robotics-cv-basics.explanation: Edge detection algorithms like Canny are specifically designed to find the boundaries and outlines of objects in an image.

robotics-cv-basics.q: A robotic arm's vision system is too slow, causing delays in picking up objects. To improve its real-time performance (increase FPS), which of the following is a common optimization strategy?
options: Increase the image resolution
Use more complex algorithms
Switch to a simpler computer vision algorithm
Process images on the robot's main CPU only
robotics-cv-basics.explanation: Using simpler algorithms, along with lower resolution and GPU acceleration, are common ways to improve the Frames Per Second (FPS) for real-time performance.

robotics-cv-basics.q: Which of these machine learning techniques is specifically highlighted in the lesson for its ability to perform *fast* object detection in computer vision?
options: Canny Edge Detection
SIFT Feature Extraction
YOLO
Template Matching
robotics-cv-basics.explanation: YOLO (You Only Look Once) is a popular machine learning-based algorithm specifically mentioned for its speed in object detection tasks.

robotics-career.q: Which career path in robotics primarily focuses on building and assembling the physical parts of a robot, like its body and circuits?
options: Software Engineering
Hardware Engineering
AI Development
Robotics Research
robotics-career.explanation: Hardware engineering involves designing and building the mechanical and electrical components that make up a robot.

robotics-career.q: For tasks like AI development, machine learning, and scripting in robotics, which programming language is most commonly in demand?
options: Java
Python
MATLAB
robotics-career.explanation: Python is widely used for AI, machine learning, and general scripting in robotics due to its extensive libraries and ease of use.

robotics-career.q: Which of these sectors is highlighted as a significant growth area for new robotics career opportunities?
options: Traditional office automation
Autonomous vehicles
Manual data entry services
Basic consumer electronics repair
robotics-career.explanation: Autonomous vehicles, along with medical robotics and collaborative robots, represent major growth sectors for robotics careers.

robotics-career.q: A robotics professional who uses tools like SolidWorks or Fusion 360 to create 3D models and test robot designs virtually before physical construction works in which area?
options: Firmware Development
Robotics Applications (e.g., manufacturing)
Design and Simulation
Electrical Engineering
robotics-career.explanation: Design and simulation roles use CAD software to model and test robot designs in a virtual environment.

robotics-competitions.q: What is a primary goal of robotics competitions like RoboRave or RoboCup?
options: To entertain large audiences with robot battles.
To challenge students to solve real-world problems.
To demonstrate advanced AI capabilities to experts.
To market new robotic products to consumers.
robotics-competitions.explanation: Robotics competitions primarily aim to challenge students to use their skills to solve practical, real-world problems.

robotics-competitions.q: Which of the following is a common challenge category found in robotics competitions?
options: Human-robot dance-offs.
Autonomous navigation.
Building custom robot manufacturing plants.
Predicting stock market trends using robots.
robotics-competitions.explanation: Autonomous navigation is a key category in robotics competitions, requiring robots to move and interact with their environment independently.

robotics-competitions.q: What valuable skill do students typically develop by participating in robotics competitions?
options: Advanced culinary arts.
Professional video editing.
Systems integration (sensors + code + mechanics).
Speed typing on a keyboard.
robotics-competitions.explanation: Participating in competitions helps students learn systems integration, which is combining sensors, code, and mechanical parts to create a functional robot.

robotics-competitions.q: Why are constraints like size, weight, and cost important factors in robotics competitions?
options: They make robots look more aesthetically pleasing.
They help prevent robots from escaping the competition area.
They force smart design choices and resource optimization.
They ensure all robots are identical for fair play.
robotics-competitions.explanation: Competition constraints encourage participants to make smart design choices and optimize their use of limited resources.

robotics-ethics.q: Which of the following is NOT typically considered one of the core ethical considerations in robotics?
options: Safety
Autonomy
Market Value
Liability
robotics-ethics.explanation: Market value is a business concern, not a core ethical consideration in robotics alongside safety, autonomy, and liability.

robotics-ethics.q: A robot's fail-safe design primarily ensures that it:
options: Always completes its assigned task without interruption.
Defaults to a safe state, such as stopping or retracting, if a system failure occurs.
Can automatically repair itself if components break down.
Operates at maximum efficiency at all times.
robotics-ethics.explanation: Fail-safe design dictates that if a system failure occurs, the robot automatically reverts to a non-hazardous state to prevent harm.

robotics-ethics.q: Why is an emergency stop (E-stop) mechanism crucial for robots?
options: To increase the robot's operating speed for faster task completion.
To allow human operators to instantly override and halt all robot motion in an emergency.
To remotely calibrate the robot's internal sensors and actuators.
To upload new programming code to the robot while it is running.
robotics-ethics.explanation: An E-stop provides a critical human override to immediately halt robot operation and prevent potential harm or accidents.

robotics-ethics.q: What is a primary real-world risk associated with physical robotic systems?
options: They can become outdated quickly due to technological advancements.
They require constant software updates and maintenance.
They can cause physical injury to people due due to their movement and power.
They are difficult to transport between different work environments.
robotics-ethics.explanation: As physical systems, robots can exert force and movement, posing a direct risk of physical injury to humans if safety protocols are not followed.

robotics-ml-intro.q: What is the primary advantage of using Machine Learning in robotics compared to traditional, rule-based programming?
options: It allows robots to execute only pre-programmed sequences.
It enables robots to learn and adapt from data without explicit rules for every scenario.
It makes robots perfectly precise in all movements.
It completely eliminates the need for any human intervention.
robotics-ml-intro.explanation: Machine learning allows robots to learn complex tasks and adapt from data, making them more flexible than robots programmed with only rigid, hardcoded rules.

robotics-ml-intro.q: A robot is learning to navigate a complex environment. It receives positive 'reward' signals when it reaches its goal and negative signals when it makes mistakes. Which type of machine learning is being primarily used?
options: Supervised Learning
Unsupervised Learning
Reinforcement Learning
Clustering Learning
robotics-ml-intro.explanation: Reinforcement learning involves an agent learning through trial and error by receiving rewards or penalties for its actions in an environment to optimize its behavior.

robotics-ml-intro.q: Which of the following is a practical application where Machine Learning would be highly beneficial for a robot, as discussed in the lesson?
options: Strictly following a pre-set, unchanging path for assembling components.
Performing real-time image classification to identify whether an object is a ball or a cube.
Executing a series of identical welding tasks repeatedly at a fixed location.
Only moving when a human operator directly controls its every joint.
robotics-ml-intro.explanation: Image classification, such as distinguishing between different object shapes, is a classic example of how machine learning helps robots perceive and understand their environment from data.

robotics-ml-intro.q: One significant challenge when implementing Machine Learning models on a physical robot is 'real-time inference.' What does this challenge primarily refer to?
options: The difficulty in gathering enough unique training data for the model.
Ensuring the ML model can process information and make decisions quickly enough for the robot to react promptly.
The problem of the robot forgetting previously learned skills over time.
The high cost associated with developing new ML algorithms.
robotics-ml-intro.explanation: Real-time inference refers to the critical need for the ML model to process input data and generate predictions fast enough for the robot to operate smoothly and respond to its environment without delay.

robotics-vision-tracker.q: What is the main purpose of a Vision-Based Tracker robot in this mini-project?
options: To navigate a maze autonomously.
To detect and follow a specific colored object.
To communicate with other robots wirelessly.
To build a map of its environment.
robotics-vision-tracker.explanation: The lesson summary states that a tracker robot uses a camera to detect and follow a colored object.

robotics-vision-tracker.q: Which combination of technologies is essential for building the Vision-Based Tracker described?
options: GPS, Lidar, and a speaker.
RFID reader, ultrasonic sensors, and a gripper.
A camera, image processing (OpenCV), and motor control.
Accelerometer, gyroscope, and a display screen.
robotics-vision-tracker.explanation: The project uses a camera for input, OpenCV for real-time image processing, and motor control (via servos/differential drive) to move the robot.

robotics-vision-tracker.q: One significant challenge when implementing a Vision-Based Tracker is:
options: The robot running out of battery power quickly.
Maintaining a stable internet connection for remote control.
The object moving closer or farther, causing its apparent size to change.
The need for advanced voice recognition capabilities.
robotics-vision-tracker.explanation: The lesson specifically lists 'scale changes (object moving closer/farther)' as a challenge for vision-based tracking.

robotics-vision-tracker.q: In the context of this Vision-Based Tracker, what is the primary role of the PID loop?
options: To identify the color of the target object.
To ensure the object remains centered in the camera's frame.
To broadcast the robot's location to other devices.
To play a sound when the object is detected.
robotics-vision-tracker.explanation: The PID loop is crucial for maintaining the object centered in the camera's frame by providing stable motor control feedback.

robotics-sumo.q: What is the primary objective of a sumo robot in a competition?
options: To collect the most objects from the ring.
To solve a complex maze within the ring.
To push its opponent out of the ring.
To display the most intricate light show.
robotics-sumo.explanation: A sumo robot's main goal is to win by pushing its competitor out of the designated ring area.

robotics-sumo.q: Which design feature is crucial for a sumo robot to achieve aggressive pushing and stability?
options: A very high center of gravity.
A lightweight chassis.
A low center of gravity.
A tall, narrow shape.
robotics-sumo.explanation: A low center of gravity provides better stability and leverage for aggressive pushing maneuvers.

robotics-sumo.q: What type of sensors are typically positioned *under* the chassis of a sumo robot to detect the ring edge?
options: Ultrasonic sensors.
Front-facing vision cameras.
Infrared (IR) sensors.
Pressure sensors.
robotics-sumo.explanation: Infrared (IR) sensors placed underneath the chassis are commonly used to differentiate between the ring surface and the area outside the ring.

robotics-sumo.q: According to the lesson summary, what is an important strategic consideration for a sumo robot regarding the ring edge?
options: To always rush towards the edge to gain momentum.
To detect the ring edge *before* losing balance.
To ignore the edge and focus solely on the opponent.
To jump over the edge if it gets too close.
robotics-sumo.explanation: An effective strategy involves using edge detection to identify the ring boundary and adjust position to avoid going out, especially before the robot becomes unbalanced.

game-p5js-intro.q: What is p5.js primarily described as?
options: A new programming language
A JavaScript library for creating interactive graphics
A software development kit (SDK) for mobile games
A web server framework
game-p5js-intro.explanation: p5.js is defined as a JavaScript library that simplifies the creation of interactive graphics.

game-p5js-intro.q: Which p5.js function is used to initialize your sketch and runs only once at the beginning?
options: draw()
loop()
setup()
start()
game-p5js-intro.explanation: The setup() function in p5.js is specifically for initializing the sketch and executes only once.

game-p5js-intro.q: Which p5.js function is responsible for rendering frames continuously, creating animation?
options: initialize()
draw()
createCanvas()
renderOnce()
game-p5js-intro.explanation: The draw() function in p5.js is called repeatedly to render new frames, allowing for continuous animation.

game-p5js-intro.q: In p5.js, what is the term for the drawing area where all your graphics and animations appear?
options: The console
The terminal
The canvas
The viewport
game-p5js-intro.explanation: The canvas is the designated drawing area within a p5.js sketch where all visual elements are displayed.

robotics-final-project.q: What is the primary goal of an "Integrated Robot" mini-project?
options: To master a single advanced robotic skill.
To design a robot that uses only one type of sensor.
To combine various learned skills like sensing, control, and decision-making.
To build the largest possible robot without budget limits.
robotics-final-project.explanation: An integrated robot project is specifically designed to combine multiple robotic skills, such as sensing, control, and decision-making, into a single functional system.

robotics-final-project.q: An autonomous delivery bot using LIDAR for navigation, a gripper, and Bluetooth communication is an example of an integrated robot because it utilizes:
options: Only very simple, single-purpose components.
Just one sensor for all tasks.
A combination of different sensor types, actuators, and communication methods.
Primarily manual control from a human operator.
robotics-final-project.explanation: This example demonstrates an integrated system by using multiple types of sensors (LIDAR), actuators (gripper), and communication (Bluetooth) to achieve complex tasks autonomously.

robotics-final-project.q: When planning an "Integrated Robot" mini-project, which of these factors is crucial to consider for a *realistic* scope, as described in the lesson?
options: Ignoring all budget constraints to achieve maximum features.
Developing the project individually in a single weekend.
Factoring in a 4-8 week development timeline, a 2-3 person team, and budget constraints.
Only using pre-built modules with no custom programming.
robotics-final-project.explanation: The lesson emphasizes that integrated robot mini-projects should have a realistic scope, including a manageable timeline (4-8 weeks), a small team (2-3 people), and awareness of budget and tool access.

robotics-final-project.q: Why is "decision-making (logic/AI)" a key component of an integrated robot project, especially for an autonomous delivery bot?
options: It makes the robot look more futuristic, but isn't functionally essential.
It's only required if the robot needs to communicate wirelessly.
It allows the robot to interpret sensor data, make choices, and react to its environment independently.
It simplifies the control system by reducing the need for multiple sensors.
robotics-final-project.explanation: Decision-making logic enables the robot to process input from various sensors, understand its environment, and autonomously determine the appropriate actions to take.

game-colors-fill.q: What is the primary color model used for defining colors in p5.js, and what is the typical range for each color component?
options: CMYK, 0-100
Hexadecimal, #000000-#FFFFFF
game-colors-fill.explanation: p5.js uses the RGB color model, where Red, Green, and Blue components each range from 0 (no intensity) to 255 (full intensity).

game-colors-fill.q: Which p5.js function should you use to set the color of the *interior* of a shape?
options: stroke()
background()
fill()
color()
game-colors-fill.explanation: The fill() function is specifically used to set the color that will fill the inside of subsequent shapes drawn.

game-colors-fill.q: To make a shape's outline completely transparent, what value should be provided for the alpha channel in the stroke() function?
options: Negative values are not allowed for alpha.
game-colors-fill.explanation: An alpha value of 0 means completely transparent, while 255 means completely opaque.

game-colors-fill.q: If you call stroke(0, 255, 0); and then rect(10, 10, 50, 50);, what color will the rectangle's outline be?
options: Red
Green
Blue
Black
game-colors-fill.explanation: In RGB, (0, 255, 0) represents maximum green and no red or blue, resulting in a pure green color.

game-canvas-coords.q: Where is the (0,0) coordinate located on a canvas?
options: The top-left corner
The bottom-left corner
The exact center of the canvas
The top-right corner
game-canvas-coords.explanation: The canvas coordinate system starts with (0,0) at the very top-left of the drawing area.

game-canvas-coords.q: If you increase the X-coordinate of an object on the canvas, which way will it move?
options: Upwards
To the right
To the left
Downwards
game-canvas-coords.explanation: On a canvas, increasing the X-coordinate moves an object horizontally towards the right.

game-canvas-coords.q: To draw an image further down on the canvas, which coordinate value do you need to increase?
options: The X-coordinate
The Y-coordinate
Both X and Y coordinates
Neither, you decrease X
game-canvas-coords.explanation: On a canvas, increasing the Y-coordinate moves an object vertically downwards.

game-canvas-coords.q: You draw a circle at coordinates (50, 75). If you want to draw a second circle slightly to its right and slightly below it, which coordinates would be appropriate?
game-canvas-coords.explanation: Moving right means increasing the X-coordinate, and moving down means increasing the Y-coordinate.

game-input-mouse.q: Which p5.js built-in variable would you use to get the current horizontal (left-to-right) position of the mouse cursor on the canvas?
options: mousePositionX
mouseX
getMouseX()
cursorX
game-input-mouse.explanation: The `mouseX` variable in p5.js continuously stores the current horizontal position of the mouse cursor relative to the canvas.

game-input-mouse.q: In p5.js, which specific function is automatically called once every time a mouse button is pressed down?
options: mouseClicked()
mouseDetect()
mousePressed()
onMouseDown()
game-input-mouse.explanation: The `mousePressed()` function is a callback function in p5.js that executes any code placed inside it whenever a mouse button is pressed.

game-input-mouse.q: To make an element follow the mouse cursor's movement across the canvas, which p5.js function would be most appropriate to place the code for updating the element's position?
options: mousePosition()
mouseMoved()
mouseOver()
mouseDrag()
game-input-mouse.explanation: The `mouseMoved()` function is called repeatedly whenever the mouse cursor moves, making it ideal for continuous tracking and response to movement.

game-input-mouse.q: According to the lesson summary, why are features like `mouseX`, `mouseY`, and the `mousePressed()` function crucial for creating games?
options: They help optimize game performance by reducing lag.
They allow the game to respond to user input, making it interactive.
They automatically generate game assets like characters and backgrounds.
They are primarily used for debugging errors in the game code.
game-input-mouse.explanation: These features are fundamental because they enable the game to detect and react to player actions, which is the core of game interactivity.

game-keyboard.q: In p5.js, what type of keyboard input does the `key` variable primarily store when a key is pressed?
options: Numerical `keyCode` values for all keys.
The character representation of printable keys (e.g., 'a', '1', space).
A boolean value indicating if any key is pressed.
Mouse click coordinates.
game-keyboard.explanation: The `key` variable holds the character value of the key that was pressed, useful for letters, numbers, and symbols.

game-keyboard.q: To detect special keys like the arrow keys (UP_ARROW, DOWN_ARROW, etc.) or the Shift key in p5.js, which variable should you primarily use?
options: The `key` variable.
The `keyCode` variable.
The `mouseButton` variable.
The `frameRate` variable.
game-keyboard.explanation: `keyCode` provides numerical values for non-character keys like arrow keys, function keys, or modifiers that don't have a printable character.

game-keyboard.q: Which p5.js function is called automatically *once* every time a keyboard key is pressed down?
options: `draw()`
`setup()`
`keyPressed()`
`mouseReleased()`
game-keyboard.explanation: The `keyPressed()` function is an event handler specifically designed to execute code when a key is pressed down.

game-keyboard.q: You want to move a character represented by a variable `playerY` upwards by 5 pixels when the 'w' key is pressed. Which p5.js code snippet, placed inside `keyPressed()`, would achieve this?
options: `if (key === 'w') { playerY += 5; }`
`if (keyCode === 'W') { playerY -= 5; }`
`if (key === 'w') { playerY -= 5; }`
`if (mouseIsPressed) { playerY -= 5; }`
game-keyboard.explanation: This code checks if the character key 'w' was pressed and then decreases `playerY` by 5 to move the character upwards on the screen (as lower Y values are higher on the screen).

game-sprite-basics.q: What is the primary role of a 'sprite' in game development?
options: To play background music for the game.
To represent interactive game elements like characters, enemies, or items.
To store the player's score and progress.
To define the overall game world's physics rules.
game-sprite-basics.explanation: Sprites are visual game objects that players interact with or observe, such as characters, items, or enemies.

game-sprite-basics.q: Based on the lesson, which set of properties commonly defines a sprite in p5.js?
options: Name, creation date, and file size.
Position, velocity, and appearance.
Sound volume, transparency, and shadow.
Score, health, and inventory.
game-sprite-basics.explanation: Sprites are typically defined by their position on the screen, how they are moving (velocity), and what they look like (appearance).

game-sprite-basics.q: Why is using 'classes' beneficial when creating multiple sprites in a game?
options: Classes reduce the overall file size of the game's assets.
Classes automatically make sprites invincible in the game.
Classes provide an efficient way to organize and create many similar sprites with shared properties and behaviors.
Classes are only used for sprites that do not move on the screen.
game-sprite-basics.explanation: Classes allow you to create a blueprint for sprites, making it efficient to generate and manage many individual sprites with consistent properties and methods.

game-sprite-basics.q: In p5.js, how are sprites generally represented or structured within the code?
options: As simple integer values that represent their ID.
As JavaScript functions that draw a static image.
As JavaScript objects, often created from a class, holding their properties and methods.
As plain text strings that describe their current state.
game-sprite-basics.explanation: In p5.js, sprites are typically represented as objects (often instances of a custom Sprite class) that encapsulate their data and behavior.

game-score-display.q: Which of the following is typically tracked as part of a game's state?
options: Player's mouse movements
The game's current score
The computer's CPU temperature
The network latency
game-score-display.explanation: The game state is used to keep track of essential information like the player's score, health, and current level.

game-score-display.q: What is the main purpose of text rendering in the context of displaying game information?
options: To play sound effects
To make background images
To show the player the score and other game data
To process user input
game-score-display.explanation: Text rendering is crucial for visually presenting information such as the player's score, current level, or health on the screen.

game-score-display.q: Which of these is an example of a common 'game state'?
options: Debugging code
Creating new assets
The 'Game Over' screen
Writing design documents
game-score-display.explanation: The 'Game Over' screen represents a distinct state the game enters, separate from gameplay, menu, or paused states.

game-score-display.q: When a player pauses the game, what usually happens to the game's state and logic?
options: The game immediately ends and restarts
The player's score is reset to zero
The game's logic and actions are temporarily suspended
All game assets are automatically deleted
game-score-display.explanation: When a game is paused, its logic and action typically halt, allowing the player to take a break or access options without disrupting the game flow.

game-velocity.q: In game development, what does an object's "velocity" primarily represent?
options: Its current location on the game screen.
The speed and direction at which it is moving.
How quickly it is accelerating or decelerating.
The total distance it has traveled since starting.
game-velocity.explanation: Velocity precisely defines both how fast an object is moving and in what direction.

game-velocity.q: How is smooth, continuous movement typically achieved for an object in a game engine each frame?
options: By randomly assigning a new position to the object.
By setting the object's position back to its starting point.
By adding the object's velocity to its current position.
By multiplying the object's current position by a small number.
game-velocity.explanation: Adding an object's velocity to its position every frame causes it to move smoothly by a consistent amount in a consistent direction.

game-velocity.q: If an object needs to "bounce" off a wall upon collision, what programming action is typically taken to change its direction?
options: Stop the object's movement entirely.
Teleport the object to a completely different area.
Reverse the component of its velocity perpendicular to the wall.
Significantly increase the object's speed.
game-velocity.explanation: Reversing the appropriate velocity component (e.g., `velocity.x = -velocity.x` for a vertical wall) makes the object bounce back.

game-velocity.q: Which statement about velocity is true in the context of game movement?
options: Velocity is the same as the object's current location.
Velocity tells you how fast and where an object is going.
Velocity only refers to an object's speed, not its direction.
Velocity is only used for objects that are accelerating.
game-velocity.explanation: Velocity combines both the magnitude (speed) and the direction of an object's movement.

game-collision.q: What is the primary purpose of collision detection in game development?
options: To make sprites look more realistic.
To determine if two game objects are touching or overlapping.
To calculate the speed of a moving object.
To change the color of a sprite when it moves.
game-collision.explanation: Collision detection's main role is to identify when game objects interact spatially by touching or overlapping.

game-collision.q: For circle-to-circle collision detection, which two pieces of information are essential to compare?
options: The area of each circle and their speeds.
The color of each circle and their textures.
The distance between their centers and the sum of their radii.
The x and y coordinates of their top-left corners.
game-collision.explanation: Circle-to-circle collision primarily relies on comparing the distance between the two circles' centers against the sum of their individual radii.

game-collision.q: In circle-to-circle collision, a collision is detected when the distance between the two circles' centers is what, compared to the sum of their radii?
options: Greater than.
Equal to.
Less than.
Greater than or equal to.
game-collision.explanation: A collision occurs when the distance separating the two circle centers is strictly less than the combined length of their radii, indicating an overlap.

game-collision.q: A game has two circular sprites. Sprite A has a radius of 5 units, and Sprite B has a radius of 3 units. If the distance between their centers is 7 units, are they colliding?
options: Yes, because 7 is greater than 5.
No, because 7 is not equal to 8.
Yes, because 7 is less than 8.
No, because 7 is greater than 3.
game-collision.explanation: The sum of their radii is 5 + 3 = 8. Since the distance (7) is less than the sum of their radii (8), the sprites are colliding.

game-enemies.q: What is the primary role of implementing Enemy AI in a game?
options: To make the game run faster on all devices.
To give enemies believable and varied behaviors within the game world.
To design the visual appearance of the game's environments.
To manage the player's score and progress.
game-enemies.explanation: Enemy AI defines how non-player characters act, react, and make decisions in the game.

game-enemies.q: How do enemies typically determine if the player is close enough to be 'sensed' or detected?
options: By randomly guessing the player's location.
By performing a distance check between the enemy and the player's position.
By waiting for the player to enter a specific cheat code.
By checking the total number of enemies in the level.
game-enemies.explanation: Distance checks are a fundamental technique used to trigger AI behaviors based on proximity to the player.

game-enemies.q: Which of these is a common 'AI state' an enemy might have, as mentioned in the lesson?
options: Its current health points.
The 'Patrolling' behavior.
The game's background music.
The player's current weapon.
game-enemies.explanation: Patrolling is a distinct AI state where an enemy moves along a predefined path, contributing to behavior variety.

game-enemies.q: Why is it useful for an enemy to have different AI states like 'Idle,' 'Patrol,' 'Chase,' and 'Attack'?
options: To reduce the amount of memory the game uses.
To make the enemy's behavior more dynamic, varied, and responsive to player actions.
To automatically generate new levels for the player to explore.
To allow the enemy to fly through walls and obstacles.
game-enemies.explanation: Using different AI states allows enemies to transition between behaviors, making interactions with the player more engaging and less predictable.

game-jumping.q: In game development, what is the primary role of 'gravity' on a character?
options: To make the character run faster.
To pull the character downwards towards the ground.
To make the character invisible.
To push the character upwards constantly.
game-jumping.explanation: Gravity is a force that consistently pulls objects downward, simulating real-world physics.

game-jumping.q: When a character 'jumps' in a game, what immediate effect does the game usually apply?
options: It instantly teleports the character to a higher position.
It applies a temporary upward velocity to the character.
It makes the character immune to damage.
It increases the character's health points.
game-jumping.explanation: Jumping typically involves giving the character an initial burst of upward velocity to counteract gravity.

game-jumping.q: After a character jumps and reaches its peak height, why does it start falling back down?
options: The character simply runs out of 'jump fuel'.
Gravity continues to pull the character down, and the initial upward velocity diminishes.
A hidden timer runs out, forcing the character down.
The game randomly decides it's time to fall.
game-jumping.explanation: Gravity continuously acts on the character, and as the initial upward velocity from the jump fades, gravity's downward pull becomes dominant, causing the fall.

game-jumping.q: In the context of jumping and gravity, why are 'platforms' often crucial in a game?
options: They make the game levels look more colorful.
They define solid ground from which a character can initiate a jump.
They automatically collect items for the player.
They instantly defeat enemies that touch them.
game-jumping.explanation: Platforms provide the solid surface or 'ground' that a character needs to be on to successfully perform a jump.

game-levels.q: What is the primary reason games often have multiple levels that progress?
options: To make the game longer and require more playtime.
To give players more opportunities to save their game progress.
To gradually introduce new challenges and increase the game's difficulty.
To allow for different artistic styles or themes in each section of the game.
game-levels.explanation: Level progression is fundamentally about introducing new challenges and increasing difficulty over time to keep the player engaged.

game-levels.q: Which of the following is a common way to increase the difficulty of a game as a player progresses to a new level?
options: Decreasing the player's starting health or resources.
Reducing the number of enemies or simplifying puzzle mechanics.
Making enemies move faster, adding more obstacles, or increasing enemy count.
Giving the player more powerful starting weapons or abilities.
game-levels.explanation: Increasing enemy speed, adding more obstacles, or increasing enemy counts are direct methods to make a new level more challenging.

game-levels.q: In a game, which of these is most likely to be defined as a 'level completion goal'?
options: Opening the game's options or settings menu.
Defeating all specified enemies, collecting all required items, or reaching a specific exit point.
Pausing the game for a short break or to read a tutorial.
Changing the game's display resolution or audio settings.
game-levels.explanation: Level completion goals are specific tasks like defeating enemies, collecting items, or reaching a destination that signify the end of a level.

game-levels.q: When a player successfully completes a level in a game, what programming action would typically be initiated to continue the game's progression?
options: Deleting the game's save file to ensure a fresh start.
Loading the game's main menu screen for the player to select a new game mode.
Loading the next level's game scene or environment data.
Quitting the application immediately, expecting the player to restart.
game-levels.explanation: Upon completing a level, the game's code typically loads the assets and setup for the subsequent level, moving the player to the next stage of progression.

game-animation.q: What is the primary method to create a visual animation in game development using frames?
options: Changing the color of a single image over time.
Moving a single image around the screen quickly.
Displaying a sequence of different images (frames) in rapid succession.
Making a single image grow and shrink repeatedly.
game-animation.explanation: Animation is achieved by showing a series of distinct images, called frames, one after another very quickly to create the illusion of movement.

game-animation.q: What is a 'sprite sheet' in the context of sprite animation?
options: A document listing all the sprites used in a game.
A single image file containing multiple frames for an animation, arranged in a grid.
A special effect applied to a sprite to make it glow.
The background image behind a character sprite.
game-animation.explanation: A sprite sheet is an efficient way to store many animation frames within one image file, often arranged in rows and columns.

game-animation.q: To make a character appear to walk smoothly across the screen using sprite animation, what action would you primarily perform with its frames?
options: Apply a blur filter to the character's image.
Continuously display the very first frame of the walk cycle.
Rapidly cycle through the different frames of the character's walk animation.
Only make the character bigger and smaller.
game-animation.explanation: Cycling through a character's animation frames one after another creates the fluid motion needed for actions like walking.

game-animation.q: Each individual picture that makes up an animation sequence is typically referred to as what?
options: A layer
A pixel
A frame
A texture
game-animation.explanation: Each distinct image in an animation sequence is called a frame, and displaying these frames rapidly creates the animation.

game-flappy-bird.q: What is the primary way a player typically makes the bird character move upwards in a Flappy Bird clone?
options: Holding down the 'up' arrow key continuously
Tapping or clicking the screen/mouse button
Moving a joystick upwards
The bird automatically ascends over time
game-flappy-bird.explanation: Flappy Bird clones use a tap-to-jump mechanic where each tap provides an upward force to the bird.

game-flappy-bird.q: In a Flappy Bird clone, how do the pipe obstacles usually appear to move?
options: They move vertically up and down in place
They scroll horizontally from right to left across the screen
The bird flies horizontally past stationary obstacles
They randomly teleport to new positions
game-flappy-bird.explanation: The obstacles in Flappy Bird clones typically scroll horizontally towards the player to create the illusion of movement.

game-flappy-bird.q: What event is described as ending the game in a Flappy Bird clone?
options: The player reaching a high score
Running out of a timer
Colliding with an obstacle or the ground
Collecting a certain number of coins
game-flappy-bird.explanation: Collision detection is key in Flappy Bird, as hitting any obstacle or the ground ends the game.

game-flappy-bird.q: Which of the following aspects of the bird's movement does the player primarily control in a Flappy Bird clone?
options: Its horizontal speed
Its color changes
Its vertical position
Its ability to shoot projectiles
game-flappy-bird.explanation: The player's main interaction is to control the bird's vertical position by tapping to make it jump.

game-particles.q: What is the primary purpose of a particle system in game development?
options: To manage enemy AI movement paths.
To create realistic physics simulations for rigid bodies.
To generate dynamic visual effects like smoke, fire, or explosions.
To store and load player save data efficiently.
game-particles.explanation: Particle systems are specifically designed to simulate complex visual effects such as explosions, smoke, or fire by emitting many small objects.

game-particles.q: According to the lesson, what is a common characteristic of the particles emitted by a particle system?
options: They always have identical properties and appearance.
They are typically very large and detailed 3D models.
They often possess random properties like size, speed, or color.
They remain visible on screen indefinitely once created.
game-particles.explanation: Particle systems emit many particles that often have random properties to create more dynamic and natural-looking effects.

game-particles.q: What happens to a particle after its specified lifetime expires within a particle system?
options: It instantly teleports to a new random location.
It continues to exist indefinitely without any change.
It is frozen in place and waits to be manually reset.
It fades out, disappears, or is recycled by the system.
game-particles.explanation: Particles within a system are designed to fade out or disappear after their predefined lifetime has expired, preventing an endless accumulation of particles.

game-particles.q: In a particle system, what component is responsible for creating and releasing individual particles into the scene?
options: The particle collector.
The particle compressor.
The particle emitter.
The particle collider.
game-particles.explanation: Particle systems 'emit' many particles, so the component responsible for creating and releasing these particles is logically called the particle emitter.

game-simple-platformer.q: What is a fundamental mechanic that defines a platformer game?
options: Complex crafting systems
Real-time strategy combat
Jumping and navigating platforms
Extensive dialogue choices
game-simple-platformer.explanation: Jumping and interacting with platforms are the central actions in nearly all platformer games.

game-simple-platformer.q: Which of these physics concepts is essential for a player character to fall back to the ground after a jump?
options: Drag
Lift
Gravity
Centrifugal force
game-simple-platformer.explanation: Gravity is the force that pulls objects downwards, making characters fall and land on platforms.

game-simple-platformer.q: If your player character keeps falling through platforms instead of landing on them, which core mechanic likely needs to be implemented or fixed?
options: Player animation system
Background music integration
Collision detection and response
User interface design
game-simple-platformer.explanation: Collision detection is what allows the game to recognize when the player character touches a platform, preventing them from falling through.

game-simple-platformer.q: In a simple platformer, what is the main purpose of "obstacles" like gaps or moving blocks?
options: To provide bonus points only.
To test the player's movement and jumping skills.
To unlock secret areas instantly.
To change the game's difficulty randomly.
game-simple-platformer.explanation: Obstacles in platformers are primarily designed to challenge the player's ability to move, jump, and time their actions effectively.

game-memory-match.q: What is the main objective of a Memory Matching Game?
options: To race against time to click all cards.
To find and pair up all identical cards.
To avoid incorrect card combinations.
To collect the most unique cards.
game-memory-match.explanation: The core goal is to successfully locate and match all pairs of identical cards on the game board.

game-memory-match.q: When two cards are flipped, what is the game's crucial next step?
options: Randomly change their positions.
Check if the two cards have matching images/values.
Immediately end the player's turn.
Add a new card to the game board.
game-memory-match.explanation: The game must compare the two revealed cards to determine if they constitute a matching pair.

game-memory-match.q: What happens to two cards if they are flipped and do NOT form a match?
options: They are permanently removed from the game.
They stay face-up until a match is found.
They typically flip back face-down after a short display time.
The player automatically wins the game.
game-memory-match.explanation: If cards do not match, they are usually hidden again so the player must remember their positions for future turns.

game-memory-match.q: From a programming perspective, what essential information should a Memory Matching Game track for each card?
options: Its color, font, and animation speed.
Its creation date and last modification time.
Its assigned value/image and its current display state (face-up/face-down).
Its network latency and server response time.
game-memory-match.explanation: The game needs to know what each card represents and whether it is currently visible to the player to manage game logic.

game-brick-breaker.q: What is the primary objective for a player in a Brick Breaker game?
options: To build new bricks on the screen
To avoid hitting any bricks with the ball
To destroy all the bricks on the screen using the bouncing ball
To catch all falling power-ups without breaking bricks
game-brick-breaker.explanation: The main goal in Brick Breaker is to destroy all bricks by hitting them with the ball.

game-brick-breaker.q: According to the lesson, what happens when the ball makes contact with a brick in a Brick Breaker game?
options: The brick's size increases
The ball stops moving immediately
The brick is typically destroyed or damaged, and the ball bounces off it
The paddle automatically moves to the location of the brick
game-brick-breaker.explanation: When the ball hits a brick, the brick is destroyed, and the ball changes direction.

game-brick-breaker.q: How does the ball generally behave when it hits walls, the paddle, or bricks in a Brick Breaker game?
options: It passes through them without changing direction
It immediately disappears from the game
It bounces off these objects, changing its trajectory
It sticks to the object it hits until the player moves it
game-brick-breaker.explanation: The ball is designed to bounce off game elements like walls, the paddle, and bricks.

game-brick-breaker.q: What is the typical consequence of the player failing to hit the ball with the paddle and letting it fall off-screen?
options: The player immediately wins the level
The player gains an extra life
The player loses one of their lives
All the bricks on the screen instantly regenerate
game-brick-breaker.explanation: Missing the ball with the paddle results in the player losing a life, as it represents a failure to keep the ball in play.

git-intro.q: What is the primary purpose of Git?
options: A program for designing user interfaces.
A tool for managing database servers.
A version control system that tracks changes to code.
An online platform for hosting finished websites.
git-intro.explanation: Git's main function is to manage and track changes in code projects over time, acting as a version control system.

git-intro.q: Priya and Arjun are working on a project together. How does Git help them collaborate without accidentally losing each other's work?
options: It automatically writes code for both of them.
It prevents them from ever making mistakes in their code.
It records every change by each person and allows merging, preventing overwrites.
It sends them alerts whenever one person starts coding.
git-intro.explanation: Git's ability to track individual changes and merge them safely is crucial for multiple developers working on the same project without overwriting each other's work.

git-intro.q: If you make a mistake in your code while using Git, what can you do?
options: You have to manually rewrite all the code from scratch.
Git allows you to go back to a previous, working version of your code.
Git automatically fixes all errors for you.
You can only delete the entire project and start over.
git-intro.explanation: Git acts like a 'time machine,' enabling you to revert your project to an earlier, stable state if you introduce errors.

git-intro.q: Besides the actual code changes, what other crucial information does Git record for each change?
options: The project's budget and estimated completion date.
WHO made the change, WHAT was changed, WHEN it was changed, and WHY.
The number of lines of code in the entire project.
The preferred programming language for the project.
git-intro.explanation: Git provides detailed historical information for every modification, including who made it, what was altered, when it happened, and the reason for the change.

game-snake.q: What causes the snake to grow longer in the 'Snake Game'?
options: Moving quickly across the screen
Eating a piece of food
Touching the game's boundary walls
Successfully avoiding obstacles
game-snake.explanation: The lesson summary states that 'Snake eats food to grow', which is the primary mechanism for increasing the snake's length.

game-snake.q: Which of these actions will *not* cause the 'Snake Game' to end?
options: The snake colliding with a wall
The snake hitting its own body
The snake eating a piece of food
The player pressing an arrow key
game-snake.explanation: Eating food is the game's objective for growth and continues the game, while hitting walls or itself are game-over conditions.

game-snake.q: How does a player typically change the direction of the snake in the game?
options: By clicking the mouse on the desired direction
By pressing the arrow keys on the keyboard
By shaking the device or game console
By using a joystick or gamepad only
game-snake.explanation: The summary specifically mentions that 'Movement direction changes with arrow keys' as the primary control method.

game-snake.q: What is the immediate consequence when the snake successfully eats food?
options: The game immediately ends
The snake shrinks in size
The snake grows longer
The food disappears, but the snake remains the same size
game-snake.explanation: As stated in the lesson, 'Snake eats food to grow,' meaning its length increases after consuming a food item.

installing-git.q: Why is it important to configure your identity (name and email) in Git after installation?
options: To secure your GitHub account with a password.
To ensure every commit you make is correctly attributed to you.
To speed up the Git installation process.
To choose which projects Git should manage on your computer.
installing-git.explanation: Configuring your identity allows Git to credit your name and email to every commit you make, answering 'Who made this change?'.

installing-git.q: What two pieces of information are essential for configuring your identity in Git?
options: Your username and password for GitHub.
Your computer's IP address and operating system.
Your full name and email address.
The project's name and its remote repository URL.
installing-git.explanation: Git requires your name and email address to correctly identify you as the author of commits.

installing-git.q: If you configure Git globally, what does this mean for your projects?
options: The configuration applies only to the current project you are working on.
The configuration applies to all Git projects on your computer.
The configuration is stored on a remote server, not your local machine.
You need to reconfigure your identity every time you start a new project.
installing-git.explanation: Global configuration means your name and email will automatically be used for all Git repositories on your computer.

installing-git.q: According to the lesson summary, what is the immediate next step Priya needs to take after successfully installing Git?
options: Create a new Git repository for her project.
Push her existing code to GitHub.
Configure her name and email for Git.
Write some code for her project.
installing-git.explanation: After installation, configuring your identity with your name and email is crucial so Git can properly attribute your future commits.

git-init.q: What is the primary action of the `git init` command?
options: It uploads your project to GitHub.
It creates a new file named 'init.txt'.
It creates a hidden `.git` folder in your project directory.
It deletes all existing files in your project folder.
git-init.explanation: `git init` creates the essential `.git` folder, which is the core of your Git repository and stores all version control information.

git-init.q: According to the lesson, how many times should you run `git init` for a single project?
options: Every time you make a change to a file.
Once, when you first start the project.
Every day to update the repository.
Never, Git handles it automatically.
git-init.explanation: You only run `git init` once per project to initialize the repository; subsequent Git commands handle ongoing version control.

git-init.q: What crucial role does the `.git` folder play after `git init` is run?
options: It serves as a temporary storage for deleted files.
It stores all the project's images and multimedia files.
It's the 'brain' that stores all the history, branches, and configuration for your Git repository.
It is a folder that needs to be manually uploaded to a server.
git-init.explanation: The `.git` folder is where Git keeps all the necessary metadata, history, and configuration to manage your project's version control.

git-init.q: After successfully running `git init` in a new project folder, what immediately starts happening?
options: Your project is automatically published online.
Git starts tracking changes in that folder.
All files in the folder are automatically backed up to a cloud service.
You are prompted to create a new user account for Git.
git-init.explanation: Once `git init` transforms a regular folder into a Git repository, Git is ready to start tracking any changes made within that folder.

git-status.q: What is the primary purpose of the `git status` command?
options: To upload changes to a remote repository like GitHub.
To create a new Git repository in the current directory.
To display the current state of your repository, including new, modified, and staged files.
To delete files from your local repository permanently.
git-status.explanation: `git status` acts as a dashboard to show what changes are present in your local repository, such as untracked, modified, and staged files.

git-status.q: Which of the following categories of files does `git status` typically display information about?
options: Only files that have already been committed.
Only files that are completely identical to the last commit.
Untracked, Modified, and Staged files.
Files that are only present on a remote server, not locally.
git-status.explanation: `git status` explicitly shows files that are untracked (Git doesn't know about yet), modified (changed but not staged), and staged (ready for the next commit).

git-status.q: Arjun and Priya have been working on some files. Before they decide to commit their changes, what command should they run to see which files are new, modified, or ready to commit?
options: `git commit -m "Their changes"`
`git add .`
`git status`
`git push`
git-status.explanation: `git status` is the command used to check the current state of the repository and identify all modified, new, or staged files before committing.

git-status.q: The lesson describes `git status` as a 'dashboard' for your project. What kind of information would `git status` *not* typically tell you?
options: Which files are currently untracked by Git.
Which files have been modified but not yet staged.
The complete history of all previous commits in the repository.
Which files are staged and ready to be committed.
git-status.explanation: While `git status` shows the current state of your files, it does not display the entire commit history; `git log` is used for that purpose.

git-commit.q: What does the `git commit` command primarily achieve?
options: It sends your changes directly to a remote repository like GitHub.
It deletes selected files from your project's history.
It saves your staged changes to your local Git history as a new snapshot.
It moves files from your working directory to the staging area.
git-commit.explanation: `git commit` takes all changes from the staging area and permanently saves them to your local repository's history.

git-commit.q: According to best practices, what should a good `git commit` message primarily explain?
options: A detailed list of every line of code that was modified.
Only the file names that were changed.
The exact date and time the commit was made.
The *reason* or *purpose* behind the changes, explaining *why* they were made.
git-commit.explanation: A good commit message clarifies the 'why' behind the changes, providing context for the project's evolution.

git-commit.q: Which of the following is the best example of a descriptive and useful `git commit` message?
options: Changes
Update files
Fixed login button alignment
More edits
git-commit.explanation: A message like 'Fixed login button alignment' is clear, specific, and explains the purpose of the change, making it easy to understand the project's history.

git-commit.q: What is a `git commit` often compared to, in the context of your project's history?
options: A temporary backup file that will be deleted later.
A permanent link to an external website.
A distinct snapshot of your project's state at a specific moment in time.
A way to only show the very first version of your project.
git-commit.explanation: Each commit acts as a snapshot, capturing the exact state of your project at the moment it was committed, allowing you to revisit or revert to any past version.

git-add.q: What is the primary purpose of the `git add` command in the Git workflow?
options: To permanently save changes to the remote GitHub repository.
To prepare changes to be included in the next commit.
To retrieve the latest changes from the remote repository to your local machine.
To delete files from your project's history.
git-add.explanation: `git add` is used to stage changes, which means selecting and preparing them to be part of the upcoming commit.

git-add.q: Arjun has modified five different files in his project. He wants to stage *all* of these changes for his next commit. Which command should he use?
options: `git commit -a`
`git add .`
`git push --all`
`git stage *`
git-add.explanation: The `git add .` command stages all changes in the current directory and its subdirectories, preparing them for the next commit.

git-add.q: Priya has changed both `header.js` and `footer.js`. She decides she only wants to commit the changes to `header.js` right now. Which command allows her to do this selectively?
options: `git commit header.js`
`git add header.js`
`git push header.js`
`git restore header.js`
git-add.explanation: Using `git add` with a specific filename allows you to stage only that file's changes, giving you control over what goes into a commit.

git-add.q: You've just finished writing some new content in your `README.md` file. What is the immediate next step you should take before you can `git commit` these changes?
options: `git push` to upload the changes.
`git pull` to get remote updates.
`git add README.md` to stage the changes.
`git remote add origin` to set up the repository.
git-add.explanation: After making changes, you must first `git add` the files to stage them, making them ready to be included in the next `git commit`.

git-log.q: What is the primary purpose of the `git log` command?
options: To create a new branch in the repository.
To view the commit history of the project.
To push local changes to a remote repository.
To stage changes before committing them.
git-log.explanation: `git log` is used to display a record of all commits, acting as the project's 'diary'.

git-log.q: How does `git log` typically order the commits it displays?
options: Alphabetically by the author's name.
From the oldest commit to the newest commit.
From the newest commit to the oldest commit.
Randomly, with no specific order.
git-log.explanation: `git log` presents commits in reverse chronological order, meaning the most recent changes appear first.

git-log.q: Which of the following pieces of information is NOT typically shown for each commit when running `git log` by default?
options: The unique commit hash.
The author of the commit.
The exact file changes made in the commit.
The commit message and date.
git-log.explanation: `git log` shows the hash, author, date, and message, but not the detailed file changes themselves without additional options or commands like `git show`.

git-log.q: According to the lesson, what is the significance of the unique hash associated with each commit?
options: It determines the size of the repository on GitHub.
It uniquely identifies every change and allows you to reference or revert to a specific point in history.
It indicates whether the commit has been pushed to a remote repository.
It specifies the programming language used in the commit.
git-log.explanation: The commit hash is crucial because it serves as a unique identifier for each change, enabling precise referencing or reverting to any historical version of the project.

git-stash.q: What is the primary purpose of using `git stash`?
options: To permanently delete uncommitted changes from your working directory.
To temporarily save your uncommitted changes and clean your working directory, allowing you to switch tasks.
To share your local changes with other developers without committing them to a branch.
To revert your repository to a previous commit, discarding all recent work.
git-stash.explanation: `git stash` is used to temporarily save your current uncommitted changes, making your working directory clean so you can switch to another task without losing your progress.

git-stash.q: After successfully running `git stash`, what is the state of your working directory?
options: It remains unchanged, showing all your modifications as before.
All your stashed changes are automatically committed to your current branch.
It becomes clean, as if you just committed your changes or started with a fresh clone, but your changes are saved elsewhere.
Only untracked files are removed, while modified tracked files remain.
git-stash.explanation: After a successful `git stash`, your working directory becomes clean, meaning all your modified tracked files and staged changes are removed from it, but safely stored in the stash.

git-stash.q: Priya stashed her feature work to fix an urgent bug. Once the bug is fixed, what command should she use to get her feature work back into her working directory?
options: `git commit -m "Restore feature"`
`git push origin feature-branch`
`git stash pop`
`git revert HEAD`
git-stash.explanation: To retrieve the most recently stashed changes back into the working directory and remove them from the stash list, Priya should use `git stash pop`.

git-stash.q: Which of the following scenarios is an ideal use case for `git stash`?
options: You have completed a feature and want to commit it to your branch.
You accidentally deleted an important file and want to recover it from the last commit.
You are working on a new feature, but an urgent bug report comes in, requiring you to switch branches and fix it immediately without committing your incomplete feature work.
You want to permanently discard all your local changes and reset your branch to its remote state.
git-stash.explanation: `git stash` is perfect for situations where you need to temporarily set aside unfinished work to address something more urgent, then return to your original task later.

git-diff.q: What is the primary purpose of the `git diff` command?
options: To upload your local changes to GitHub.
To show line-by-line differences between versions of files.
To delete files that are no longer needed in the repository.
To create a new branch for a new feature.
git-diff.explanation: `git diff` is used to display the specific line-by-line changes that have occurred between different versions of your code.

git-diff.q: When `git diff` shows changes, what symbol typically indicates a line that has been removed?
options: A green `+` sign.
A red `-` sign.
A yellow `~` sign.
A blue `>` sign.
git-diff.explanation: `git diff` commonly uses a red `-` sign to indicate lines that have been removed from a file.

git-diff.q: According to the lesson summary, when is a particularly useful time to run `git diff`?
options: After you have already pushed your changes to GitHub.
Before initializing a new Git repository.
Before committing your changes, to review what you're about to save.
When you want to permanently delete your commit history.
git-diff.explanation: It is very useful to run `git diff` before committing to review your changes and ensure you are only committing the intended edits.

git-diff.q: If Priya modifies her `README.md` file and then runs `git diff` before making a new commit, what will it compare?
options: It will compare her current `README.md` with the version on GitHub.
It will show a list of all files in her project, without differences.
It will compare her current `README.md` with the last committed version of the file.
It will display the entire content of the `README.md` file without highlighting changes.
git-diff.explanation: `git diff` when run without arguments compares the current working directory changes to the last committed version of the files.

gitignore.q: What is the main purpose of creating a `.gitignore` file in a Git repository?
options: To list all files that should always be included in every commit.
To specify which files and directories Git should explicitly *not* track.
To define which operating system Git should run on.
To automatically compress all project files before committing.
gitignore.explanation: A `.gitignore` file is used to tell Git which specific files or patterns of files should be ignored and excluded from version control tracking.

gitignore.q: Based on the lesson, which type of file would be a *most* appropriate candidate to add to your `.gitignore` file?
options: The main source code file for your application (e.g., `main.py`).
A file containing sensitive API keys and passwords (e.g., `.env`).
A `README.md` file that explains your project.
A `package.json` file that lists project dependencies.
gitignore.explanation: Sensitive data like API keys and passwords, often stored in `.env` files, should always be excluded from Git for security reasons.

gitignore.q: Priya and Arjun add `node_modules/` to their `.gitignore` file. What is the immediate effect of this action?
options: Git will automatically install all the packages listed in `node_modules/`.
The `node_modules/` directory will be deleted from their local filesystem.
Git will stop tracking the `node_modules/` directory, making it cleaner and smaller.
Git will always include the `node_modules/` directory in every commit.
gitignore.explanation: Ignoring `node_modules/` prevents Git from tracking the many temporary and often large files within it, keeping the repository size manageable and clean.

gitignore.q: You accidentally committed a file containing your database password. What is the crucial next step *before* pushing your changes to GitHub?
options: Add the password file to `.gitignore` and commit that change.
Immediately push your changes to GitHub and then try to delete the file on GitHub.
Delete the password from Git history to prevent it from ever being pushed to the remote repository.
Rename the file that contains the password to something else.
gitignore.explanation: If a secret is accidentally committed, it must be deleted from Git history *before* pushing to prevent the sensitive information from being exposed on GitHub.

git-checkout.q: What is the primary function of the `git checkout <branch-name>` command?
options: To delete the specified branch from your repository.
To upload your local changes to a remote repository like GitHub.
To switch your working directory to match the code of the specified branch.
To merge the specified branch into your current branch.
git-checkout.explanation: `git checkout` changes the files in your working directory to reflect the state of the chosen branch.

git-checkout.q: Arjun uses `git checkout login-feature` after being on the `main` branch. What happens to the files in his local folder?
options: The files remain unchanged, but the branch name in Git is updated.
All local files are deleted, requiring a fresh clone of the repository.
The files are updated to display the code specific to the `login-feature` branch.
A new separate folder is created for the `login-feature` branch, duplicating the repository.
git-checkout.explanation: When switching branches with `git checkout`, Git updates all files in your folder to match the code of the target branch.

git-checkout.q: The lesson mentions that `git switch` is a newer command. What is its relationship to `git checkout` in the context of switching branches?
options: `git switch` is a deprecated command, and `git checkout` is the only modern way to switch.
`git checkout` is specifically for creating new branches, while `git switch` is for changing existing ones.
They serve the same primary purpose of switching branches, with `git switch` being a newer alternative.
`git switch` only works with remote branches, whereas `git checkout` works with local branches.
git-checkout.explanation: Both `git checkout` and `git switch` perform the same function of changing your active branch and updating your working directory.

git-checkout.q: Why is it described as 'fast and safe' to switch branches using `git checkout`?
options: Because it only changes the branch name without affecting any files.
Because Git intelligently tracks the history of each branch and updates only necessary files efficiently.
Because it automatically pushes all uncommitted changes to a remote server before switching.
Because it creates a full backup of your entire repository before every switch.
git-checkout.explanation: Git's understanding of each branch's history allows it to quickly and safely update your working directory with the correct files.

merge-conflicts.q: What is the primary reason a Git merge conflict occurs?
options: A developer forgets to commit their changes.
Two developers modify different files at the same time.
Two developers make different changes to the exact same part of the same file.
A developer tries to push changes without pulling first.
merge-conflicts.explanation: Merge conflicts happen when Git cannot automatically reconcile different changes made to the same lines of code in the same file by different contributors.

merge-conflicts.q: When a merge conflict occurs, which set of special markers does Git insert into the conflicted file to highlight the divergent changes?
options: `[CONFLICT START]`, `[CONFLICT DIVIDER]`, `[CONFLICT END]`
`HEAD`, `origin/main`, `feature/branch`
merge-conflicts.explanation: Git uses `<<<<<<<`, `=======`, and `>>>>>>>` to clearly delineate the conflicting sections within a file.

merge-conflicts.q: After Git detects a merge conflict, what is the immediate action a developer typically needs to take to resolve it?
options: Immediately delete the entire conflicted file.
Manually edit the conflicted file to remove Git's special markers and choose which code to keep.
Revert all local changes and pull the latest version from the remote repository.
Run `git commit -m "Fixed conflict"` without making any file edits.
merge-conflicts.explanation: Resolving a merge conflict primarily involves opening the conflicted file, manually deciding which changes to keep, and then removing the conflict markers.

merge-conflicts.q: Based on the lesson, how should you view merge conflicts in a team programming environment?
options: As a critical error that indicates a major problem with teamwork.
As a rare event that only happens if Git is misconfigured.
As a normal and expected part of collaborative development, requiring manual intervention.
As an automatic process that Git always resolves without user input.
merge-conflicts.explanation: Merge conflicts are a common occurrence in collaborative development and are a normal part of the process that requires manual resolution.

git-merge.q: What is the primary purpose of the `git merge` command?
options: To create a new branch from an existing one.
To integrate changes from one branch into another.
To remove a branch from your local repository.
To upload your local code to a remote GitHub repository.
git-merge.explanation: `git merge` is used to combine the changes made on one development line (branch) into another.

git-merge.q: Following best practices mentioned, when should Priya merge her `homepage-feature` branch into `main`?
options: Before she starts working on the feature.
After the feature is complete and thoroughly tested.
When she wants to temporarily save her work on the feature branch.
To move the `main` branch's changes into her `homepage-feature` branch.
git-merge.explanation: The lesson states that feature branches are typically merged back into `main` after testing is complete.

git-merge.q: If Priya merges her `homepage-feature` branch into `main` and there are *no conflicting changes*, what will Git do?
options: Git will stop the process and require Priya to manually resolve non-existent conflicts.
Git will automatically combine the changes from `homepage-feature` into `main`.
Git will create a new separate branch for the combined changes.
Git will erase all changes made on the `homepage-feature` branch.
git-merge.explanation: Git is designed to automatically combine changes when no conflicts are present, simplifying the merge process.

git-merge.q: Which statement accurately describes a 'merge commit' strategy as opposed to a 'fast-forward' merge?
options: A 'merge commit' creates a simple linear history without any new commit.
A 'merge commit' specifically preserves the history of the merged branch by creating a new commit.
A 'merge commit' only occurs when there are conflicts between branches.
A 'merge commit' is an older strategy that is no longer recommended by Git.
git-merge.explanation: A merge commit explicitly records the merge event in the history, preserving the branch's distinct lineage, while fast-forward creates a linear history.

git-branch.q: What is the primary purpose of creating a Git branch?
options: To permanently delete old code from the project.
To upload your code directly to GitHub without reviewing.
To establish an independent line of development for a new feature or fix.
To instantly merge all current changes into the main codebase.
git-branch.explanation: A branch serves as an independent line of development, allowing you to work on new features or changes without affecting the main, stable code.

git-branch.q: If you are working on a new feature in a branch called 'login-feature', what happens to the 'main' branch?
options: The 'main' branch is temporarily deleted until 'login-feature' is complete.
Any changes you make in 'login-feature' are automatically applied to 'main' as well.
The 'main' branch remains unaffected by the changes you make in the 'login-feature' branch.
The 'main' branch automatically merges with 'login-feature' after a set time.
git-branch.explanation: Branches allow independent work, meaning changes in one branch (like 'login-feature') do not affect another branch (like 'main') until you explicitly merge them.

git-branch.q: Priya creates a 'homepage' branch to redesign the homepage, and Arjun creates a 'login-feature' branch to build login functionality. What is true about their work?
options: Priya's changes on 'homepage' will automatically appear on Arjun's 'login-feature' as they are created.
They must take turns working on the same branch to avoid conflicts.
They can work independently without their changes interfering with each other until they are merged.
Both branches are automatically deleted once they complete their respective tasks.
git-branch.explanation: Branches enable team members like Priya and Arjun to work independently on different features without their changes immediately affecting one another.

git-branch.q: Which Git command would you typically use to create a new branch called 'new-feature' AND switch your working directory to it immediately?
options: git branch new-feature
git checkout new-feature
git checkout -b new-feature
git merge new-feature
git-branch.explanation: The `git checkout -b <branch-name>` command is a convenient shortcut that both creates a new branch and switches your current working directory to it.

git-cherry-pick.q: What is the primary purpose of `git cherry-pick`?
options: To merge all changes from one branch into another.
To undo the latest commit on the current branch.
To apply one specific commit from another branch to your current branch.
To create a new branch from an existing commit.
git-cherry-pick.explanation: Cherry-picking is designed to apply a single, specific commit from one branch onto another without merging the entire source branch.

git-cherry-pick.q: Arjun committed a critical bug fix to the `main` branch. He now needs this exact fix on the `release-v1` branch without bringing over any other new features from `main`. Which Git command should he use?
options: `git merge main`
`git cherry-pick <commit-hash-of-fix>`
`git rebase main`
`git reset --hard <commit-hash-of-fix>`
git-cherry-pick.explanation: `git cherry-pick` is the correct command for selectively applying a single commit from one branch to another without merging the whole branch.

git-cherry-pick.q: When you cherry-pick a commit from `branch-A` onto `branch-B`, what happens to `branch-A`?
options: `branch-A` is automatically merged into `branch-B`.
The cherry-picked commit is removed from `branch-A`.
`branch-A` remains unchanged.
`branch-A` is deleted.
git-cherry-pick.explanation: Cherry-picking only copies the commit's changes to the target branch; the source branch remains completely unaffected.

git-cherry-pick.q: What is a key benefit of using `git cherry-pick` instead of `git merge` for applying a bug fix from `main` to a `release` branch?
options: It is always faster than merging.
It automatically resolves all merge conflicts.
It allows you to selectively apply only specific commits, avoiding unwanted changes from the entire source branch.
It only works on remote repositories.
git-cherry-pick.explanation: The main advantage of `git cherry-pick` is its ability to bring in only specific commits, preventing the integration of an entire branch's potentially unwanted changes or history.

git-rebase.q: What is the primary purpose of `git rebase` according to the lesson?
options: To combine multiple branches into one with a merge commit.
To undo the last commit on your current branch.
To rewrite your branch's commit history on top of another branch, avoiding a merge commit.
To fetch the latest changes from a remote repository.
git-rebase.explanation: Git rebase rewrites history to make your commits appear as if they were made after the target branch, keeping a clean, linear history without a merge commit.

git-rebase.q: Priya has 3 commits on her feature branch. She wants to use `git rebase` onto `main`. What is a key outcome of this action?
options: It will create a new merge commit on the `main` branch.
Her 3 commits will be deleted from the feature branch.
Her 3 commits will appear as if they were made *after* `main`'s latest commit, keeping a linear history.
The `main` branch will be overwritten with her feature branch's history.
git-rebase.explanation: Rebasing 'replays' a branch's commits on top of another, making them appear as if they were made later and maintaining a linear history.

options: When you want to clean up your local commit history before pushing.
When your commits are already pushed to a public repository and others might be working from them.
When you are working alone on a private feature branch.
When you want to avoid a merge commit.
